description: Bean qou-wgnx. Identifies the BASIS-INVARIANT C1 connection datum chi = P00 P11/(P01 P10), the cross-ratio of the connection matrix. 0-side rebasing scales P's ROWS by elliptic functions and inf-side rescaling scales its COLUMNS, and the cross-ratio is invariant under both. On the real axis chi = exp(2i(arg c+ - arg c-)) with |chi| = 1 exactly. This also settles the [-1] artifact pole: it CANNOT be removed by renormalising the character (any multiplier-t character is theta_p(cz)/theta_p(cz/t), so varying c only MOVES the pole to [-1/c], and the rebasing ratio drags in a further pole at [-t]) — but it does not need to be, because [-1] is common to a ROW of P and therefore cancels between numerator and denominator of chi. Verified: P entries diverge to 1e73 at the artifact pole while |chi| stays exactly 1, and chi is numerically identical across c in {1, 1.7, 0.43, 2.9}. ALSO RECORDED: Mathlib at HEAD has the additive two-variable Jacobi theta but NO Jacobi triple product and no theta zero-locus results, so the converse of the Lean zero-locus lemma cannot be closed by reuse. Stokes multipliers remain OPEN.

verdict: The basis-invariant connection datum is the CROSS-RATIO chi = P00 P11/(P01 P10), invariant under both 0-side rebasing (which scales P's rows by elliptic functions) and inf-side rescaling (which scales its columns). On the real axis it is a pure phase, chi = exp(2i(arg c+ - arg c-)), |chi| = 1 exactly. The [-1] pole is NOT removable by renormalising the 0-side character — that only relocates it to [-1/c] and adds one at [-t] — but it is invisible to chi, cancelling between numerator and denominator; confirmed by chi being identical for every c tested while P itself diverges at that point. Separately recorded: Mathlib has no Jacobi triple product and no theta zero-locus results, so the converse of the Lean lemma is not cheap. STOKES MULTIPLIERS REMAIN OPEN — chi is the invariant they must be functions of, not the multipliers themselves. Nothing wired to production.
